newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt calls for interest in AIDC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt calls for interest in AIDC.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday it was calling for expressions of interest in the total acquisition of investment bank AIDC Ltd.
"This is the first time formal action has been taken to seek expressions of interest in AIDC Ltd," Finance Minister John Fahey said in a statement.
"The government is confident of finalising the sale before the end of the (1996/97) financial year."
The former Labor government previously sold off a 20 percent stake in AIDC before buying it back earlier this year when it realised it would be more attractive to sell the whole company.
The current Liberal-National government revealed its intention to sell AIDC in its pre-election policy statement.
Fahey said the government had been working with the company since the March 2 election to determine how the privatisation should proceed.
AIDC primarily provides project and structured finance services and development capital to medium sized infrastructure projects and resources companies.
Expressions of interest must be received by January 27 next year, Fahey said.
The office of asset sales would manage the sale, with corporate finance firm Phoenix Securities, assisted by Ord Minnett Corporate Finance, appointed as business advisers to the sale.
